content: 1. The study by Zurovac et al. (2013) investigated the ownership and utilization of mobile phones among healthcare workers, caregivers of sick children, and adult patients in Kenya through a cross-sectional national survey. The findings were published in Global Health. 2. Crawford et al. (2014) compared the effectiveness of SMS versus voice messaging for delivering maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) communication in rural Malawi. The study assessed delivery success and user experience, with results published in Global Health Science and Practice. 3. Fetters, Curry, and Creswell (2013) outlined principles and practices for achieving integration in mixed-methods research designs. Their work, published in Health Services Research, provides a framework for combining qualitative and quantitative approaches effectively. 4. Gilson et al. (2011) emphasized the importance of social science in building the field of health policy and systems research. Their article, published in PLoS Medicine, highlights the role of interdisciplinary approaches in advancing health systems. 5. Smith, Rosenzweig, and Schmidt (2010) discussed best practices for reporting participatory action research (PAR), advocating for a balance between detailed data and broader context. Their recommendations were published in The Counseling Psychologist. 6. Israel et al. (2008) addressed critical issues in developing and adhering to community-based participatory research (CBPR) principles. This work is included in the book Community-Based Participatory Research for Health: From Processes to Outcomes. 7. The WHO Evaluation Practice Handbook provides comprehensive guidance on evaluation methodologies, emphasizing the importance of structured approaches to assess health interventions. 8. Pritchett, Samji, and Hammer (2013) introduced the concept of structured experiential learning to explore design spaces in health program implementation, as detailed in their publication by the Center for Global Development. 9. Drummond et al. (2005) presented methodologies for conducting economic evaluations of healthcare programs in their book published by Oxford University Press. 10. Gartlehner et al. (2006) proposed criteria to distinguish between effectiveness and efficacy trials in systematic reviews, with a focus on healthcare interventions. This work was published by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. 11. Rychetnik et al. (2002) developed criteria for evaluating evidence on public health interventions, emphasizing the need for rigorous assessment. Their findings were published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. 12. Curran et al. (2012) introduced hybrid research designs that integrate clinical effectiveness and implementation research to enhance public health impact. Their work appeared in Medical Care. 13. Brown and Lilford (2006) conducted a systematic review of the stepped wedge trial design, highlighting its applications and limitations. The review was published in BMC Medical Research Methodology. 14. Grimes and Schulz (2002) discussed the strengths and limitations of descriptive studies, including cohort and case-control designs, in The Lancet. 15. Gordis (1988) provided a foundational resource on epidemiology in his book, A Dictionary of Epidemiology, published by Oxford University Press. 16. Donalek (2004) explored the process of selecting qualitative research traditions in Urologic Nursing, offering guidance for researchers in the field. 17. Lindquist (2016) provided an accessible introduction to qualitative research designs, emphasizing their application in health research. 18. Neill (2016) analyzed professional literature on qualitative research, offering insights into methodologies and their practical applications. 19. Harris et al. (2004) examined the use and interpretation of quasi-experimental studies in infectious diseases, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 20. Mann (2003) reviewed observational research methods, including cohort, cross-sectional, and case-control studies, in Emergency Medicine Journal. 21. Habicht, Victora, and Vaughan (1999) proposed evaluation designs for assessing public health program performance, published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 22. Peters, Tran, and Adam (2013) authored a practical guide on implementation research in health, published by the World Health Organization. 23. Meadows (2003) introduced qualitative research methods in British Journal of Community Nursing, providing a foundational overview for new researchers. 24. Creswell (2003) detailed research design approaches, including qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods, in his book published by SAGE Publications. 25. Mack et al. (2016) developed a field guide for qualitative research methods, offering practical tools for data collection and analysis. 26. Stewart et al. (2008) discussed qualitative research methods in dentistry, focusing on interviews and focus groups, in the British Dental Journal. 27. Burnard et al. (2008) provided strategies for analyzing and presenting qualitative data in the British Dental Journal. 28. Kadam and Bhalerao (2010) explained sample size calculation methods in International Journal of Ayurveda Research, emphasizing their importance in study design. 29. Schueren (2016) provided an overview of survey methodologies, highlighting their applications in health research. 30. The Johns Hopkins School of Public Health Open Courseware (2012) offered insights into survey research design, emphasizing practical considerations for implementation. 31. The PRISM Framework was adapted to assess routine health information system performance, providing a structured approach to data quality assessment. 32. The Green Book (2003) by HM Treasury outlined appraisal and evaluation methods for public sector business cases, emphasizing value delivery. 33. Kumar, Williams, and Sandy (2006) discussed methods for evaluating the economics of healthcare in the European Journal of Orthodontics. 34. Cunningham (2001) introduced economic evaluation concepts in healthcare, as published in the Journal of Orthodontics. 35. Robinson (1993) provided an overview of cost-benefit analysis in healthcare, published in the BMJ. 36. Dobrev et al. (2016) developed a methodology for evaluating the socio-economic impact of interoperable electronic health record (EHR) systems. 37. The OneHealth Tool by WHO-CHOICE supports cost-effectiveness and strategic planning for health interventions. 38. The ISPOR Budget Impact Analysis Good Practice II Task Force (2014) outlined principles for conducting budget impact analyses in healthcare. 39. The Economic Impact of eHealth report summarized methods, case studies, and results for evaluating digital health interventions. 40. The Green Book (2003) by HM Treasury provided supplementary guidance on delivering public value through spending proposals.
